fields.label: Intro sentence
paragraphs: A plain moulded rubber pad that carries load and holds a gap — the closed shape, where a slot or an angle is not wanted. Specified on the load it takes and the deflection you can allow, not on hardness alone, because a pad’s stiffness comes from its proportions as much as its compound. EPDM as standard.

fields.label: Two problems, one of them structural
paragraphs: 🛑 The heading and the control contradict each other. A buyer who selects NBR on a page called “EPDM Pad” is holding something the page cannot name. Renaming the page to what the part does fixes this in one move — the selector becomes a real choice and EPDM becomes the recommendation.

🛑 Natural rubber is not offered, and on a load-bearing pad it has the best fatigue resistance and the least creep of the eight. EPDM is the right default for weather; it is not the right default for sustained load, and the page cannot say so while it is named after EPDM.
Margo produces every part in every compound it mixes (client-instructed 2026-09-02). Nothing is removed — all eight are ranked, and the four missing from the live selector are added.

fields.label: Selector
columns: Why, for a flat packing pad
rows: The general-purpose answer and correctly pre-selected. Weather, ozone, UV, water and steam, and it stays flexible cold. Creeps more than natural rubber under sustained load, so allow for it in the deflection
Where the pad carries sustained load. Best fatigue resistance, highest resilience and least creep of the eight, so the gap stays held. Not for oil, and it perishes in prolonged sunlight
The compromise where the pad is both loaded and exposed — good fatigue life with reasonable weathering
Where the pad sits in oil. Poor ozone resistance, so not for an exposed position
Low-cost enclosed packing. Fatigue life below natural rubber and no oil resistance
High temperature. Low tear strength and poor fatigue resistance make it a weak choice under load
Expensive sealing compounds with no fatigue or creep advantage in a packing pad

fields.label: Cards ×4
rows: The compound is not what makes one pad different from another — the shape is. Any pad in this range can be moulded in any of the eight compounds we mix, so tell us the duty and we will name the material.
Hardness will not tell you how it behaves

Rubber bulges rather than compresses, so a thin wide pad is far stiffer than a thick narrow one of the same compound. Send the load and the deflection you can allow, and we set the shape and the hardness together.
Weather or load — they pull apart

EPDM survives sunlight and ozone; natural rubber holds a gap without creeping. Where the pad is exposed and loaded we quote neoprene and explain the trade rather than defaulting to whichever we mixed last.
Holes moulded in, not punched after
Fixing holes formed in the tool are cleaner and stronger than holes cut afterwards, and the pad keeps its full section around them. Send the bolt pattern with the outline.

fields.label: Why industries are the right frame here
paragraphs: A flat packing pad is the most generic part in the catalogue. It is not tied to a vehicle or a machine — anywhere two components need spacing, isolating or protecting from each other, this is the part. So the industry grid is the correct frame; it needs industries that actually buy packing rather than a list that includes aerospace.

sections.title: From compound to certification
sections.chip: Moulded holes and load testing are the missing steps
sections.live: LIVE H2 → From Compound to Certification · six steps · the same text as all 31 pages

fields.label: Steps
rows: Material compounding — polymer blending, additive integration and batch QC in our in-house lab. The compound is chosen for creep resistance first, since a packing pad has to hold its gap for years.

Mould design and CNC tool manufacture, in-house, held as a controlled record. Footprint and thickness are set together to reach the load and deflection, and fixing holes are formed in the tool rather than cut afterwards.
Post-cure and trimming, with adhesive backing applied where specified.
Quality inspection — dimensional check, hardness, and load-deflection tested on batch samples against the approved drawing.

Export packaging — industrial packing with documentation. Pads are packed flat and unloaded, since rubber stored under compression takes a set before it is ever fitted. ISPM-15 treated pallets where timber packaging is used.
fields.note:
Six steps, six kept. The live text says “ISO-certified lab” in step 01, which becomes “in-house lab”; step 04 is “Post-Cure & Trimming” and gains the adhesive-backing operation.
Step 02 carries the moulded-hole argument as a production fact rather than a marketing claim, which is where it is most credible.
Step 05 is what turns load and deflection from a promise into a controlled characteristic, and it is the check an industrial buyer will ask about

notes: The process block must render from the part record.
“Load-deflection tested on batch samples” is the credibility line on any load-bearing part.
